newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Foreigners sell T$14 bln Taiwan stocks in two days.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners sell T$14 bln Taiwan stocks in two days.

text.p: Profit-taking foreign institutions sold T$14.03 billion worth of Taiwan stocks in the past two days, exchange officials said on Wednesday.

Statistics released by the Taiwan Stock Exchange Corp showed that foreign institutional investors bought T$3.01 billion worth of local shares on Tuesday, but sold T$9.99 billion worth of stocks on that day, with a net selling of T$6.98 billion.
On Wednesday, it also sold T$4.04 billion worth of shares, but bought T$1.92 billion worth of stocks, with a net selling at T$2.12 billion, the statistics showed.
Total net-selling by foreign insitutions stood at T$19.73 billion from July 1 to July 23, with these investment organisations buying T$41.53 billion and selling T$61.26 billion worth of shares.
"Net-selling by foreign institutions was one major reason for the sharp falls in the local bourse on Tuesday and Wednesday," Lei Pei-yu, analyst of Pacific Securities said.
He said the net-selling triggered heavy sell-offs by local investors.
Heavy profit-taking on Taiwan's bullish electronic shares eroded early gains on Tuesday and Wednesday, pushing the benchmark stock index down 283.37 points and 169.34 points, respectively.
Brokers said foreign institutions had begun to sell the bellwether electronics to take profits, following a recent bull run on the sector.
Electronics rose well over 100 percent in the first half of 1997, taking a firm lead of the market's wider rally, but have consolidated since July 17.
